legenda: 1897 board: a deep-water harbor serves ships drawing at least 30 ft.
texto_para_tela: DEEP-WATER: AT LEAST 30 FT · 18 OR 20 FT AT HIGH WATER
nota: Calado (draft) contra profundidade: o 30 é calado de navio; o 18–20 de Mendell é a água que ele esperava na maré alta. A comparação da voz ('a ceiling of twenty feet, in a trade that was heading for thirty') junta os dois, e a fonte de 1897 (26–28 pés comuns, vapores de 30 ou mais) sustenta o 'heading for thirty'.
narracao: So that is what his "never" measured: not the bay, the estuary. In 1897, the federal board that chose the harbor's site would define a deep-water harbor as one for ships drawing at least thirty feet. A ceiling of twenty feet, in a trade that was heading for thirty. The same letter pointed next door. San Pedro Bay, Mendell wrote, was "worthy of improvement," though he questioned whether an artificial harbor there was worth it, and he asked for a survey.
